% Synthetic fixture: the path keys and scopes a sketch reaches for — a
% rounded box, a scope shifted, scaled and turned in the order its keys are
% written, a scope's colour and width ending with it, an arc continued by
% a line, an arrow stopped short of its target, and a fill at a third of
% its alpha. Invented content and design.
\documentclass{article}

\pictures{ tool = none }

\fonts{ dir = "fonts", body = "Source Serif Pro" }

\palette{
  wash = #2A6F4E,
}

\title{Scopes and Corners}
\author{Pat Placeholder}

\begin{document}

\maketitle

\section{Moved and turned}

\begin{tikzpicture}
  \draw[rounded corners=3pt] (0,0) rectangle (3,1.5);
  \node at (1.5,0.75) {box};
  \begin{scope}[shift={(4,0)}, rotate=30, wash, thick]
    \draw (0,0) -- (1,0) -- (1,1);
    \node[above] at (1,1) {turned};
  \end{scope}
  \begin{scope}[xshift=7cm, scale=0.5]
    \draw (0,0) arc (180:0:1) -- (2,-1);
  \end{scope}
  \draw[->, shorten >=2pt] (0,-1) -- (3,-1);
  \fill[fill opacity=0.3, wash] (4,-1.5) rectangle (6,-0.5);
\end{tikzpicture}

\end{document}
